name: Kerr-de Sitter and Kerr-anti-de Sitter Black Holes
description: The rotating black hole in a universe with a cosmological constant of either sign, which Brandon Carter found in 1968 among the spacetimes whose geodesic equations separate. With $\Lambda > 0$ an inner horizon, an event horizon, and a cosmological horizon surround the ring singularity, and with $\Lambda < 0$ its boundary is a rotating Einstein universe.
convention: The mass enters as the length $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the rotation parameter $a$ is a length, and the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ takes either sign, with $\Lambda = -3/\ell^2$ for Kerr-anti-de Sitter. The horizons are the real roots of $\Delta_r$, $r_- < r_+$ and, for $\Lambda > 0$, $r_c$ beyond them and $r_n$ at negative values, with surface gravities $\kappa_-$, $\kappa_+$, $\kappa_c$, and $\kappa_n$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: The universe is accelerating and its black holes spin, so the black hole of astrophysics, followed out to cosmological distances, rotates in de Sitter space [akcay2011]. Brandon Carter had shown that the Hamilton-Jacobi equation for the geodesics of Kerr's black hole separates, and that observation prompted a search for every spacetime with the same property [carter1968, carter1968separable]. He asked for two commuting symmetries and for the Klein-Gordon equation to separate as well, "not because there is any good physical reason for doing so but because it leads to a very simple algebraical form for the metric" [carter1968separable]. Einstein's equations, with or without a cosmological constant $\Lambda$, then gave every unknown function of the metric as a polynomial of at most fourth degree [carter1968separable]. Kerr's black hole sits in the most general of his families at $\Lambda = 0$, and of the members with $\Lambda \neq 0$ he wrote in 1968 that the generalisation "appears to be entirely new" [carter1968separable].¶Switch on a mass, a spin, and $\Lambda$ in that family and out comes a rotating black hole in a universe with a cosmological constant, Kerr-de Sitter for $\Lambda > 0$ and Kerr-anti-de Sitter for $\Lambda < 0$ [akcay2011, henneaux1985]. The metric looks like Kerr's in Boyer and Lindquist's coordinates with one new constant, $\Xi = 1 + \Lambda a^2/3$, which keeps the axis free of conical singularities [hawking1999rotation, akcay2011]. Could complex coordinate transformations of Schwarzschild's solution have found it? Marek Demiański tried in 1973, reached a class of metrics that "does not contain a Kerr type solution with cosmological constant", and derived the metric again from Carter's separable form [demianski1973]. A small cosmological constant leaves the black hole's horizon "only slightly displaced", he showed, and a positive one in today's sign adds a second horizon far away, at $r \sim \sqrt{3/|\Lambda|}$ [demianski1973].¶Can a black hole spin faster than Kerr allows? In de Sitter space it can [akcay2011]. A positive $\Lambda$ gives the hole up to four horizons: an inner and an outer one, $r_-$ and $r_+$, a cosmological horizon $r_c$ far outside, and a second cosmological horizon at negative $r$, beyond the ring singularity [akcay2011, lake2015]. Black holes exist up to $a = 1.101\,GM/c^2$, reached at $\Lambda = 0.1777\,(c^2/GM)^2$, and for a larger $\Lambda$ none exists [stuchlik2004]. Where $\Lambda > c^4/(9G^2M^2)$ no Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole exists, so a black hole there "must be spinning" [akcay2011]. Drawn along the axis, the conformal diagram "continues ad infinitum in all directions", and Jack Borthwick built the whole extension in 2018 by following the light rays that fall straight in and climb straight out [akcay2011, borthwick2018].¶Kerr-anti-de Sitter is the model isolated system of anti-de Sitter space: Marc Henneaux and Claudio Teitelboim took it in 1985, in a frame that does not rotate at infinity, as "the prototype which all isolated systems in anti-de Sitter space approach at infinity" [henneaux1985]. Its boundary is a rotating Einstein universe, and in 1999 Stephen Hawking, Christopher Hunter, and Marika Taylor-Robinson set the black hole beside a conformal field theory living there: the action of the one and the partition function of the other diverge alike as the boundary's rotation reaches the speed of light [hawking1999rotation]. Can you tap a spinning black hole in a box? A wave that takes energy from the spin is reflected back by the boundary and amplified again, so the tap would run away [hawking2000]. While the boundary rotates slower than light a Killing vector field is timelike everywhere outside the horizon, and Hawking and Harvey Reall concluded in 2000 that "Energy cannot be extracted from the hole: it is classically stable" [hawking2000]. Small holes, with $r_+ \ll \ell$, do run away: Vitor Cardoso and Óscar Dias followed the growing wave through the wave equation in 2004 [cardoso2004kads].¶Which mass does such a black hole have? Measured against anti-de Sitter space it is $M/\Xi^2$, with angular momentum $aMc/\Xi^2$ [henneaux1985, gibbons2005firstlaw]. With that mass, and with the horizon's angular velocity measured against the frame that does not rotate at infinity, the first law of thermodynamics holds [caldarelli2000, gibbons2005firstlaw]. With $M/\Xi$ and the angular velocity against a frame that rotates at infinity it fails, and the right side of the law "is not even an exact differential" [gibbons2005firstlaw]. Carter had noticed that his metric is de Sitter space plus the square of a null vector, and Gary Gibbons, Hong Lü, Don Page, and Christopher Pope used that in 2004 to carry it to every dimension [gibbons2004prl, gibbons2005kds]. They quote Carter's verdict on his own solution, from his Les Houches lectures: "Although I don't think that there is much physical justification for believing a non-zero $\Lambda$ term, it is perhaps worth quoting the result as a geometrical curiosity" [gibbons2005kds].¶Is the black hole stable? For $\Lambda > 0$ and slow rotation it is: a theorem of Peter Hintz and András Vasy, published in 2018, takes initial data close to those of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole, with no symmetry assumed, to a metric that settles exponentially fast on a Kerr-de Sitter black hole of nearby mass and spin [hintz2018kds]. With $\Lambda < 0$ the boundary sends every wave back, and a Klein-Gordon field outside the hole decays only as a power of the logarithm of time [holzegel2013decay, holzegel2014]. Gustav Holzegel and Jacques Smulevici, who proved it, conjectured that "Kerr-AdS spacetimes are dynamically unstable for generic perturbations" [holzegel2013decay]. Inside the hole, Óscar Dias, Felicity Eperon, Harvey Reall, and Jorge Santos found in 2018, every Kerr-de Sitter black hole short of extremal has modes that decay slowly enough to respect strong cosmic censorship [dias2018]. De Sitter space can also make such black holes in pairs, and the two of a pair spin in opposite directions [booth1999].

related.text: Carter's black hole with the cosmological constant switched off. At $\Lambda = 0$ the cosmological horizon is gone and $\Xi = \Delta_\theta = 1$.
Kerr-de Sitter with the spin switched off, $a = 0$ and $\Lambda > 0$. Kottler's two horizons are what is left of $r_+$ and $r_c$.
Kerr-anti-de Sitter with the spin switched off, $a = 0$ and $\Lambda = -3/\ell^2$. Its boundary is an Einstein universe at rest.
Kerr's black hole with a charge where this one has a cosmological constant. Both sit in the family Carter found by asking the Hamilton-Jacobi equation to separate [carter1968separable].
Kerr-de Sitter with the mass taken out, $r_s = 0$ and $\Lambda > 0$. The rotation parameter $a$ is left over as a choice of spheroidal coordinates, which Akcay and Matzner untwist [akcay2011].
Kerr-anti-de Sitter with the mass taken out, $r_s = 0$ and $\Lambda < 0$, which is anti-de Sitter space in unusual coordinates [henneaux1985].

The rotating black hole of anti-de Sitter space in three dimensions. Hawking, Hunter, and Taylor-Robinson set its boundary, a rotating Einstein universe as well, beside this one's [hawking1999rotation].
The black hole of de Sitter space with a charge where this one has a spin. Its horizons are arranged the same way, an inner one, an outer one, and a cosmological one [lake2015].
A black hole with an acceleration where this one has a spin. Plebański and Demiański put both, and the cosmological constant, into one family of solutions [kamran2009, plebanski1976].
Kerr's black hole with a NUT parameter where this one has a cosmological constant. Carter's separable family holds both [carter1968separable, bini2003].

domains: \Delta_r = 0 \;\text{(the event horizon } r_+ \text{ and, for } \Lambda > 0 \text{, the cosmological horizon } r_c\text{)}

parameters.description: Mass parameter as a length, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$; the mass measured against the de Sitter or anti-de Sitter background is $M/\Xi^2$
Rotation parameter, a length; the angular momentum is $J = aMc/\Xi^2$, and $a = 0$ is Kottler's metric
Cosmological constant, an inverse length squared, of either sign: Kerr-de Sitter for $\Lambda > 0$, Kerr for $\Lambda = 0$, and Kerr-anti-de Sitter for $\Lambda = -3/\ell^2 < 0$, where $|a| < \ell$
Keeps the axis free of a conical singularity with the azimuthal angle periodic in $2\pi$
Vanishes on the ring singularity, $r = 0$ on the equator

Equal to $\Xi$ on the axis and to $1$ on the equator

coordinates.convention: We use Carter's metric in the coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Hawking, Hunter, and Taylor-Robinson, which are Boyer and Lindquist's at $\Lambda = 0$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$, and write $\Xi$, $\rho$, $\Delta_r$, and $\Delta_\theta$ as the parameters define them. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \Phi)$ with $\Phi = \phi - a\Lambda ct/3$, the angle of Henneaux and Teitelboim's frame that does not rotate as $r \to \infty$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and write $\Xi$, $\rho$, $\Delta_r$, and $\Delta_\theta$ as the parameters define them. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

nonzero.value: \dfrac{9r_s\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 6\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\left(r^2 + a^2\right) + 3\Lambda\,a^2\,r_s\left(3r^4\cos^2\theta - 2r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^4\theta - a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta - a^4\cos^4\theta\right) - 2\Lambda^2\,a^2\,r\,\rho^4\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}{18\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_r}

\dfrac{9r_s\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 6\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\left(r^2 + a^2\right) + 3\Lambda\,a^2\,r_s\left(3r^4\cos^2\theta - 2r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^4\theta - a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta - a^4\cos^4\theta\right) - 2\Lambda^2\,a^2\,r\,\rho^4\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}{18\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_r}

geodesics: \ddot{t} + \dfrac{9r_s\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 6\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\left(r^2 + a^2\right) + 3\Lambda\,a^2\,r_s\left(3r^4\cos^2\theta - 2r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^4\theta - a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta - a^4\cos^4\theta\right) - 2\Lambda^2\,a^2\,r\,\rho^4\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}{9\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_r}\dot{t}\dot{r} - \dfrac{2a^2\left(3r\,r_s\,\Delta_\theta + \Lambda\,\Xi\,\rho^4\right)\sin\theta\cos\theta}{3\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{t}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{a\,r_s\left(3r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\,r^2 - a^4\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_r}\dot{r}\dot{\Phi} + \dfrac{2a^3\,r\,r_s\sin^3\theta\cos\theta}{\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{\theta}\dot{\Phi} = 0

coordinates.convention: We use ingoing Kerr coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \tilde\phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, $dr_*/dr = (r^2 + a^2)/\Delta_r$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$, and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi + a\Xi\,dr/\Delta_r$, and write $\Xi$, $\rho$, $\Delta_r$, and $\Delta_\theta$ as the parameters define them.
geodesics: \ddot{v} + \dfrac{\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r_s\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 2\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\right)}{6\rho^6}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{2a^2\left(3r\,r_s + \Lambda\,\rho^4\right)\sin\theta\cos\theta}{3\rho^4\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{v}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{a\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r_s\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 2\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\right)\sin^2\theta}{3\Xi\,\rho^6}\dot{v}\dot{\tilde\phi} - \dfrac{2a^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\rho^2\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{2a\,r\sin^2\theta}{\Xi\,\rho^2}\dot{r}\dot{\tilde\phi} - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}{\rho^2\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{2a^3\,r\,r_s\sin^3\theta\cos\theta}{\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{\theta}\dot{\tilde\phi} - \dfrac{\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r\,\Xi\,\rho^4 - a^2\,r_s\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{2\Xi^2\,\rho^6}\dot{\tilde\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.convention: We use outgoing Kerr coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \tilde\phi)$, with the retarded time $u = ct - r_*$ a length, $dr_*/dr = (r^2 + a^2)/\Delta_r$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$, and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi - a\Xi\,dr/\Delta_r$, and write $\Xi$, $\rho$, $\Delta_r$, and $\Delta_\theta$ as the parameters define them.
geodesics: \ddot{u} - \dfrac{\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r_s\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 2\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\right)}{6\rho^6}\dot{u}^2 - \dfrac{2a^2\left(3r\,r_s + \Lambda\,\rho^4\right)\sin\theta\cos\theta}{3\rho^4\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{u}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{a\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r_s\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right) - 2\Lambda\,r\,\rho^4\right)\sin^2\theta}{3\Xi\,\rho^6}\dot{u}\dot{\tilde\phi} + \dfrac{2a^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\rho^2\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{2a\,r\sin^2\theta}{\Xi\,\rho^2}\dot{r}\dot{\tilde\phi} + \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}{\rho^2\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{2a^3\,r\,r_s\sin^3\theta\cos\theta}{\Xi\,\rho^4\,\Delta_\theta}\dot{\theta}\dot{\tilde\phi} + \dfrac{\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r\,\Xi\,\rho^4 - a^2\,r_s\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{2\Xi^2\,\rho^6}\dot{\tilde\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.convention: We use the Kerr-Schild coordinates $(\tau, r, \theta, \psi)$ of Gibbons, Lü, Page, and Pope, with $c\,d\tau = c\,dt + r_s r\,dr/((1 - \Lambda r^2/3)\Delta_r)$ and $d\psi = d\phi - (a\Lambda/3)\,c\,dt + a r_s r\,dr/((r^2 + a^2)\Delta_r)$, and write $\Xi$, $\rho$, $\Delta_r$, and $\Delta_\theta$ as the parameters define them. We take components in the chart $x^0 = c\tau$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{\tau}$ means $d(c\tau)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{\Delta_\theta}{\Xi}\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda r^2}{3}\right)c^2\,d\tau^2 + \dfrac{\rho^2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda r^2}{3}\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}dr^2 + \dfrac{\rho^2}{\Delta_\theta}d\theta^2 + \dfrac{r^2 + a^2}{\Xi}\sin^2\theta\,d\psi^2 + \dfrac{r_s r}{\rho^2}\left(\dfrac{\Delta_\theta}{\Xi}c\,d\tau + \dfrac{\rho^2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda r^2}{3}\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}dr - \dfrac{a\sin^2\theta}{\Xi}d\psi\right)^2

nonzero.value: \dfrac{2r\,\Xi\,\rho^4\left(3 - \Lambda\,r^2\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - a^2\,r_s\left(3 - \Lambda\,r^2\right)\left(3r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\,r^2 - a^4\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta - 3a^2\,r\,r_s^2\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{2\Xi\,\rho^4\left(3 - \Lambda\,r^2\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{2r\,\Xi\,\rho^4\left(3 - \Lambda\,r^2\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - a^2\,r_s\left(3 - \Lambda\,r^2\right)\left(3r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\,r^2 - a^4\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta - 3a^2\,r\,r_s^2\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{2\Xi\,\rho^4\left(3 - \Lambda\,r^2\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

-\dfrac{a\,r_s\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta + 3a^2\right) + 3a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta + \Lambda\,a^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r^2\cos^2\theta - r^2 + 2a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)\cot\theta}{6\Xi\,\rho^6\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{a\,r_s\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta + 3a^2\right) + 3a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta + \Lambda\,a^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r^2\cos^2\theta - r^2 + 2a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)\cot\theta}{6\Xi\,\rho^6\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

-\dfrac{\Delta_\theta\left(r\,r_s\left(r^2 - 3a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta + 3a^2\right) + 3a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta + \Lambda\,a^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r^2\cos^2\theta - r^2 + 2a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right) + 2\Lambda\,\rho^6\left(\Xi\,\rho^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta\right)\right)}{6\Xi^2\,\rho^6\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{\Delta_\theta\left(r\,r_s\left(r^2 - 3a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta + 3a^2\right) + 3a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta + \Lambda\,a^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r^2\cos^2\theta - r^2 + 2a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right) + 2\Lambda\,\rho^6\left(\Xi\,\rho^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta\right)\right)}{6\Xi^2\,\rho^6\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{\Delta_\theta\left(r\,r_s\left(r^2 - 3a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta + 3a^2\right) + 3a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta + \Lambda\,a^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r^2\cos^2\theta - r^2 + 2a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right) + 2\Lambda\,\rho^6\left(\Xi\,\rho^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta\right)\right)}{6\Xi^2\,\rho^6\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

-\dfrac{\Delta_\theta\left(r\,r_s\left(r^2 - 3a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(2r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta + 3a^2\right) + 3a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta + \Lambda\,a^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(3r^2\cos^2\theta - r^2 + 2a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right) + 2\Lambda\,\rho^6\left(\Xi\,\rho^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - a^2\,r\,r_s\sin^2\theta\right)\right)}{6\Xi^2\,\rho^6\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}
